question: In 1931, who recognised that an aromatic compound must have an odd number of pairs of electrons, which can mathematically be written as 4n + 2 (n = 0, 1, 2, 3 etc.)?
solution:
The correct answer is __Erich Huckel__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Erich Huckel was a German chemist and physicist.
 
• He proposed a theory in 1931 to help determine if a planar ring molecule would have aromatic properties.
 
• Erich Huckel recognized that an aromatic compound must have an odd number of pairs of electrons.
 
• His rule states that a cyclic, planar molecule is considered aromatic if it has 4n+2 pi electrons.
 
• This rule is known as Huckel's Rule.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pi bond:- Bond formed by the same phase overlap of atomic orbitals along a direction perpendicular to the internuclear axis is called pi bond.
 
• Pi electrons:- An electron that resides in the pi bond (s) of a double bond or a triple bond or in a conjugated p orbital is called pi electron.
 
• ​System is divided into aromatic, anti-aromatic, and non-aromatic based on no. of pi electrons-
 
 
• ​​​Aromatic system - The number of pi electrons in an aromatic system is determined by N = 4n+2 (n is an integer)
 
• Anti-aromatic system - The number of pi electrons in an anti-aromatic system is determined by N = 4n (n is an integer)
 
• Non-aromatic - If a compound does not have a continuous ring of conjugated p orbitals in a planar module, then it is called non-aromatic.
